channel.title: Spatium Novum
channel.description: Models, and where they break. Commodity trading, finance, machine learning, pharmacology, economics, cognition.

item.title: From the Frontier to the Market
item.description: Markowitz asked how one investor should choose given a set of beliefs. CAPM asked which expected returns could survive when everyone's holdings had to add up to the market.

item.title: Five Hundred Years of Data
item.description: Harry Markowitz formalised the second stage of portfolio choice in 1952. The first stage was deciding what to believe about the future.

item.title: Where the Proof Runs Out
item.description: The same local solver can report success at $0, $100 and $400 on one small continuous problem. Only a valid bound can say which answer is global.

item.title: When the Answer Is Yes or No
item.description: Half a warehouse is not a warehouse. That innocent fact changes both the answer and the proof.

item.title: Optimising Against a Guess
item.description: The optimum of a model is the optimum of your estimates. Those are not the same thing.

item.title: Rows, Columns, and What They Cost
item.description: Stigler's diet has 77 choices and nearly half a trillion candidate column sets. It still solves in milliseconds.

item.title: The Last Place "Optimal" Means Anything
item.description: OPTIMIZE is the motto of the age. In one discipline the word still means something you can prove, and in 1947 that proof cost 120 man-days.

item.title: The Swiss Commodity Trading World, on Two Axes
item.description: One of the oldest industries there is, and one of the least documented. An interactive map that puts every kind of actor on a grid of what they do against what they move, so you can see where a firm like Trafigura actually sits.
